summary: North Dakota household of 2 (you and your partner), no children, no one working. One member is 65 or older. Reported Social Security of about $55k–$75k a year, other income of about $50k a year, and $25k–$40k in bank accounts and investments. No one is pregnant and no one is a full-time college student. Household income is well above the limits for all ten listed programmes: SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the child tax credit, ACA premium tax credit (about 400% of the federal poverty level for a 2-person household is roughly $86k, and counted income is above that), and free school meals. No programme on the list appears to apply. Because the answers needed some re-matching, please check these figures if your situation has changed. Medicare, which is not on this list, may be relevant for the 65+ member and is worth checking separately.
